vote.question: FUTARCHY CONDITIONAL RESOLUTION [US-IA U.S. Senate]: Ashley Hinson Arenholz (R) has accumulated $46,267,212 in career FEC-reported receipts (anchored this cycle by Elon Musk ($168,000,000) and $386,907,000 from top-5 patrons)—out-raising general opponent Joshua Turek ($24,290,521) by 1.9x—exhibiting the "Extractive Energy & Petrochemical Capture" profile. Will independent constituent & oracle review confirm that this private-interest capital concentration compromises public representation in US-IA, thereby executing the IA Corrective Restitution Pool toward clean water remediation, community grid resilience, and environmental health clinics?
vote.futarchy_thesis: Private campaign financing treats US-IA representation as an investable asset class. When Ashley Hinson Arenholz's campaign apparatus absorbs $46,267,212 (anchored this cycle by Elon Musk ($168,000,000) and $386,907,000 from top-5 patrons), policy incentives skew toward regulatory leniency toward industrial emissions, grid monopolies, and watershed externalities. This futarchy market converts spectator outrage into direct fiscal counter-leverage.
options: Yes — Confirm Capture & Execute State Restitution Bounty
No — Veto Capture Claim & Roll Escrow Pool to Bipartisan Commons
Abstain — Log On-Chain Constituent Dissent Only

outcomes.YES_EXECUTE_RESTITUTION: Confirms special-interest capture; releases 100% of escrowed pool to audited state 501(c)(3) restitution beneficiaries — direct corrective remediation of the captured constituent impact.
outcomes.NO_VETO_BENEFICIAL_COMMONS: Finds representation uncompromised by top-donor concentration; redirects 100% of escrowed pool to a bipartisan, district-wide beneficial common good (e.g., voter-protection legal defense, disaster-relief matching fund, or civic-infrastructure project) where both sides of the political divide can agree that the community as a whole is strengthened — countering zero-sum capture politics with positive-sum community investment.
outcomes.ABSTAIN_AUDIT_ONLY: Logs cryptographic constituent dissent on-chain without shifting conditional odds; preserves the pool for future cycle reconsideration.

If the Yes option wins, funds fund front-line clean water remediation, community grid resilience, and environmental health clinics restitution beneficiaries. If the No option wins, funds redirect to a bipartisan district-wide common good that strengthens the entire community — denying special interests the ability to commandeer the bounty and promoting positive-sum governance over zero-sum subjugation.
